A bad battery will not hold a charge.
A bad regulator will cause low output.
A bad connection will cause a parasitic draw and prevent charging.
A parasitic draw will cause the battery to be drained.
questions.explanation: A bad alternator, loose belt, bad battery, bad regulator, corroded terminal or parasitic draw can all cause these problems with the charging system.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is exhibiting a complex set of problems, including blowing warm air, the compressor clutch engaging and disengaging rapidly, fluctuating refrigerant pressures, an unusually high low-side pressure, an unusually low high-side pressure, a hissing sound coming from the evaporator area, an unusual amount of moisture or condensation on the dashboard vents, and an intermittent clicking noise from the compressor, and also the air flow from the vents is weak. Which of the following components or conditions could be contributing to this wide range of problems?
answers: A leak in the evaporator core
feedbacks: A bad expansion valve can cause all the pressure and cooling issues.
A bad low pressure switch can cause cycling.
A clogged drier will cause high pressure.
A failing compressor will cause low pressure.
A leak will cause a hissing sound and low pressure.
A faulty clutch will cause a clicking noise.
questions.explanation: A bad expansion valve or low-pressure switch, clogged drier, failing compressor, leak in the evaporator or a bad compressor clutch can cause all of these complex issues with the AC system.

questions.question: A vehicle’s ABS (Anti-lock Braking System) warning light illuminates intermittently, and a scan tool shows a C1095 code.  The code indicates a fault in a specific wheel speed sensor circuit, but the sensor itself tests good. What is the MOST likely cause of this issue?
answers: A damaged or corroded connector or wiring
feedbacks: Although a faulty ABS control module can cause ABS light issues, it’s less likely given the specific wheel speed sensor code and sensor test.
The wheel speed sensor tests good.
A damaged or corroded connector can cause an open or short circuit, leading to an intermittent signal issue even with a good sensor.
Low brake fluid can trigger the brake warning light, but not specifically an ABS issue related to a wheel speed sensor.
questions.explanation: The most likely cause is a wiring or connector fault that would cause an intermittent issue with a good sensor.

questions.question: A vehicle with a high-performance engine exhibits knocking and pinging under heavy acceleration, even when using premium fuel. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of this issue?
feedbacks: Incorrect ignition timing is a common cause of knocking and pinging.
Faulty O2 sensors typically cause fuel mixture issues, not directly causing knocking.
A dirty air filter would cause a rich mixture, not typically knock.
Low oil level will cause serious damage, and not usually knocking.
questions.explanation: Incorrect ignition timing often results in knocking because the combustion is not occurring at the correct moment.

questions.question: A vehicle’s automatic transmission shifts harshly and sometimes slips between gears. The fluid level is correct, and the fluid is not burnt. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: A malfunctioning solenoid in the valve body
feedbacks: The fluid level is correct.
The TPS is related to engine performance, not internal transmission issues.
A malfunctioning solenoid can cause incorrect shifts and slippage.
Worn transmission bands cause slipping, but don't often shift harshly.
questions.explanation: Faulty solenoids cause incorrect pressures within the transmission which causes harsh shifts and slippage.

questions.question: A hybrid vehicle displays a P0A80 code, indicating a ‘Replace Hybrid Battery Pack’ error. After replacing the battery pack, the code reappears. What is the next step?
answers: Reset the HV system's DTCs and relearn the system.
feedbacks: The BMS should be tested but is not the next logical step after a new battery.
The system needs to be cleared of previous codes, and often relearning is required.
The inverter is related to voltage, not battery management.
The wiring would need to be tested before replacing.
questions.explanation: It is imperative that you clear the codes and relearn the system after replacing a hybrid battery.

questions.question: A vehicle has a parasitic drain, causing a dead battery overnight. After performing a parasitic draw test, it’s found that a relay in the fuse box is drawing excessive current even when the car is off. What is the best way to identify which specific circuit that relay controls?
answers: Check the vehicle’s electrical wiring diagrams.
Use a multimeter to trace the circuit path.
Disconnect relays, one at a time, to see which drops the draw.
feedbacks: That would be an expensive and inaccurate guess.
Wiring diagrams provide the component the relay controls.
Although that is an option, it would be time-consuming and less accurate than the diagrams.
This would not identify what the circuit is for.
questions.explanation: The electrical wiring diagrams will help identify the component controlled by the relay in question.

questions.question: A diesel engine runs rough and produces excessive black smoke. Fuel pressure tests normal, but there is a lack of power. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
feedbacks: The crankshaft position sensor would cause starting or stalling issues.
Dirty or leaking injectors will cause poor fuel atomization leading to black smoke.
A bad EGR valve could cause a no start, but would not cause excessive black smoke.
A restricted exhaust will cause low power and may cause white smoke.
questions.explanation: Dirty or leaking injectors will cause poor atomization which in turn leads to unburnt fuel and black smoke.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is blowing warm air. The compressor clutch engages, and refrigerant pressures are within normal range, but the low side pressure is higher than usual. What is the MOST probable cause of this problem?
answers: A weak or broken compressor reed valve
feedbacks: The expansion valve causes a drop in pressure, leading to cold air.
A clogged receiver drier would cause a restriction, leading to high high-side pressure.
A blend door actuator controls hot and cold air blending.
Compressor valves control internal pressure, and will lead to high low-side pressure.
questions.explanation: A failing reed valve in the compressor will cause the low side to not be at the proper pressure.

questions.question: A vehicle equipped with a direct injection engine exhibits misfires only when the engine is cold. The spark plugs and coils are new, and fuel pressure is within specs. What is the MOST likely cause of the misfire?
answers: Carbon buildup on the intake valves
feedbacks: A crankshaft sensor failure causes stalling and starting issues.
Direct injection engines often have carbon buildup which can cause misfires when cold.
A knock sensor will not cause misfires when cold.
A leaking EGR will cause rough running, and not necessarily misfires.
questions.explanation: Carbon buildup on the intake valves in direct injected engines will often cause misfires upon cold start.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system whines loudly when turning the steering wheel, and there’s noticeable resistance. The power steering fluid level is correct. What is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: A loose drive belt would cause a whining noise, but not resistance in the steering wheel.
A faulty power steering pump will cause the whining noise and steering resistance.
Worn steering rack bushings would cause loose steering, and not usually noise.
The power steering fluid level is correct.
questions.explanation: A faulty power steering pump is the cause of the whining and resistant steering.

questions.question: A vehicle has been recently serviced.  The client reports that a ‘check engine’ light has come on shortly after leaving. When the fault codes are checked, it is seen that code P0420 has been stored. What is the most probable cause for this?
answers: A faulty oxygen sensor after the catalyst
feedbacks: A faulty fuel pump usually does not generate this fault code
This code specifies a problem with the catalyst, but the post catalyst sensor could be the cause
The P0420 code specifically mentions an issue with the catalytic converter.
The mass air flow sensor usually leads to a different error code.
questions.explanation: The P0420 code specifies an issue with the catalytic converter and should be investigated further.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic throttle control system has a P2111 error code which refers to the electronic throttle actuator being stuck in the open position. The fault is intermittent. Which of the following is the MOST likely cause of this issue?
answers: A faulty accelerator pedal position sensor
A loose or corroded connector on the electronic throttle body
feedbacks: A faulty APP sensor will affect the throttle response, but not necessarily cause this error.
A bad connection can cause the throttle body to be stuck open.
The MAF sensor will not cause this issue.
A bad ECU is not the most likely cause.
questions.explanation: The most common cause of this intermittent fault is a bad connection at the throttle body.

questions.question: A vehicle's suspension system causes a clunking noise when going over bumps. The shock absorbers test fine. What is the MOST probable cause of the clunking noise?
answers: Worn or loose sway bar bushings or end links
feedbacks: Worn strut mounts will cause noise, but usually not clunking.
Worn bushings and end links are a common cause of clunking sounds.
Ball joints can cause noise, but usually a squeak.
Wheel bearings cause a constant hum.
questions.explanation: Worn sway bar end links or bushings are the most common reason for a clunking noise in suspension.

questions.question: A vehicle's charging system has a low voltage output, and the battery light is on. The battery is new, and the connections are clean and tight. What is the most likely cause?
answers: A bad voltage regulator in the alternator
A blown fuse in the charging circuit
feedbacks: A failing regulator is the most common reason for the lack of charging.
A blown fuse will cause a complete lack of charging.
A bad starter will not affect the charging system.
A bad ignition switch would cause starting and ignition issues.
questions.explanation: A bad voltage regulator will cause a low output from the alternator.

questions.question: A vehicle with a dual-clutch transmission (DCT) exhibits harsh shifting and occasional slipping. The fluid level is good, and the fluid looks clean. What is the MOST likely cause of the shifting issue?
feedbacks: Input and output speed sensors would not cause the issues.
Worn clutch packs or forks will cause harsh shifting and slipping.
The throttle position sensor affects the engine.
A bad TCU is less common and less likely than clutch issues.
questions.explanation: The most common issues with dual clutch transmissions is the wear on the clutches and forks.

questions.question: A vehicle has a very high fuel consumption and runs very rich. The engine is running smoothly, but the smell of fuel is apparent. What is the most likely cause of the problem?
answers: A faulty Mass Air Flow Sensor
feedbacks: A faulty MAF sensor will often cause a lean condition and not a rich one.
Leaking injectors will cause a rich running condition and the smell of fuel.
A faulty O2 sensor will usually cause a lean or fluctuating condition.
A faulty coolant temperature sensor would cause a misfire or no-start.
questions.explanation: Leaking injectors will cause excessive fuel to enter the engine, causing a rich condition and the smell of fuel.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronically controlled air suspension system displays a fault code related to the ride height sensor on one corner. The sensor itself tests good. What is the MOST likely cause of the problem?
answers: A broken or damaged linkage on the ride height sensor
A leak in the air spring
feedbacks: A faulty compressor would cause all of the corners to be low.
A broken linkage will give a false reading to the ride height sensor.
A leak will lower the affected corner, not necessarily cause a sensor fault.
A faulty air control module will cause other issues also.
questions.explanation: The most common cause of a ride height sensor issue, when the sensor is ok is a faulty linkage.

questions.question: A vehicle’s TPMS (Tire Pressure Monitoring System) warning light illuminates, indicating a low tire pressure on one tire.  The tire is properly inflated, and the sensor itself tests good with a scan tool. What is the next best troubleshooting step?
answers: Check for interference from aftermarket electronics
Recalibrate the TPMS sensors using the scan tool
Inspect the wiring harness and connector for damage
feedbacks: The sensor tests good, and should not be the first action.
Aftermarket electronics can interfere with the system.
TPMS sensors may require calibration, but not if it's a bad reading.
A damaged wiring or connector is the next most common cause for the issue.
questions.explanation: The most likely cause of a bad reading from a good sensor, after inflation, is an electrical issue.

questions.question: A vehicle equipped with lane departure warning system (LDWS) gives intermittent error messages despite clear road markings. The camera lenses are clean and undamaged. What is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: The steering angle sensor is used to see where the vehicle is steering, but not necessarily the road.
The forward-facing camera for lane departure might be out of alignment.
Radar sensors are usually for collision avoidance.
The camera lenses are clean, so the windshield is the problem.
questions.explanation: The most common issue with intermittent LDWS errors is a misaligned camera.

questions.question: A vehicle has a slow but steady coolant leak. After inspecting all hoses, clamps, the water pump and the radiator, no leaks can be found. What is the most likely location of the leak?
feedbacks: A cracked cylinder head would cause other more significant issues.
A slow coolant leak, without external evidence, is often the heater core.
A leaking oil cooler will not usually leak coolant.
A faulty thermostat housing is visible, and not usually slow.
questions.explanation: A leaking heater core will cause an internal leak of coolant into the passenger compartment and no evidence on the ground.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system activates inappropriately at low speeds and on smooth roads. No fault codes are stored in the system. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: A faulty ABS wheel speed sensor
feedbacks: A bad speed sensor will usually register an error code.
A misaligned steering angle sensor will tell the ESC that the steering is inconsistent.
A faulty lateral sensor will cause intermittent issues.
A bad yaw sensor will not usually cause intermittent problems.
questions.explanation: An incorrect steering angle sensor signal will cause the system to think the car is turning more than it actually is.

questions.question: A modern car has a problem with the stop/start system not engaging. The battery is fully charged, and the check engine light is not illuminated. The vehicle has been driving for over 15 minutes. What is the most common reason?
answers: An issue with the brake pedal switch
feedbacks: This will affect the starting of the engine, and not start/stop.
The brake pedal switch is needed for the system to work.
A faulty BMS will often stop the system from working.
The TCM affects shifting, and will not stop start/stop.
questions.explanation: The two most common reasons for stop/start problems, without an error code, are the battery management sensor or the brake pedal switch.

questions.question: A vehicle with a manual transmission has a hard time getting into certain gears, particularly second and third gear, and there is grinding when trying to engage them. What is the MOST likely cause of this issue?
feedbacks: A worn clutch will not usually cause grinding.
Worn synchros will cause grinding of specific gears.
Worn input shaft bearings will cause whine and not grinding.
A sticking clutch master will affect all gears.
questions.explanation: Worn synchros are the usual culprit of grinding when shifting into certain gears.

questions.question: A vehicle's rear brakes lock up excessively during light braking.  The ABS light is not illuminated, and the front brakes work fine.  What is the MOST likely cause of this problem?
answers: A faulty rear wheel speed sensor
feedbacks: A faulty proportioning valve is the most likely culprit for rear brake lockup.
A bad ABS module will usually illuminate a warning light.
A faulty speed sensor will cause ABS issues and usually light.
Sticking calipers cause drag and heat, not locking up.
questions.explanation: A faulty proportioning valve can cause a lack of brake force on the front brakes, causing the rears to lock up first.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system has a low refrigerant charge. After a vacuum test, it holds vacuum, and no leaks are visible. What is the most likely cause of the low charge?
answers: A slow leak in the evaporator core
The low pressure switch is faulty
feedbacks: Evaporators can leak internally and are hard to locate.
A compressor seal will usually cause external signs of leakage.
A bad expansion valve does not cause a loss of refrigerant.
A faulty low-pressure switch will not usually cause loss of refrigerant.
questions.explanation: A common cause of slow refrigerant loss is a leak in the evaporator, which is located in the dashboard.

questions.question: A vehicle’s electric power steering (EPS) system is intermittently cutting out, making the steering heavy. There are no fault codes stored. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: A loose or corroded connector on the EPS motor
feedbacks: A bad connection is the most common culprit.
A faulty steering angle sensor will usually register an error code.
A low system voltage will cause other warning lights to illuminate.
A faulty torque sensor would not cause a complete loss of power.
questions.explanation: A bad connection will cause an intermittent loss of power to the steering.

questions.question: A modern vehicle with keyless entry has a 'no key detected' error intermittently despite a new battery in the fob. What is the next best troubleshooting step?
answers: Test the voltage output of the fob with a multimeter
Check the vehicle’s antenna locations and wiring
feedbacks: The battery was just replaced.
A voltage test may not be accurate.
A broken wire or faulty antenna could cause the issues.
Replacing the fob is a last resort option.
questions.explanation: The most common issue with keyless entry is a fault antenna or bad connection.

questions.question: A vehicle's four-wheel-drive (4WD) system engages but makes a loud grinding noise when attempting to turn sharply on dry pavement. What is the MOST likely cause of this noise?
answers: The vehicle is in 4WD on dry pavement
feedbacks: A worn chain will cause slipping, and not usually grinding.
A faulty actuator will cause a no-engagement issue.
Four-wheel-drive vehicles bind on dry pavement and grind when turning sharply.
A bad differential will cause grinding even in straight line driving.
questions.explanation: Four-wheel drive vehicles should only be used on loose surfaces. Binding will cause grinding when turning on dry surfaces.

questions.question: A vehicle with a manual transmission has excessive clutch pedal travel and a soft, spongy feel. The clutch does not slip, and the clutch fluid level is correct. What is the MOST likely cause of this problem?
feedbacks: A worn throwout bearing will cause noise and not a soft pedal.
A sticking master cylinder will cause a soft or spongy pedal feel.
A worn pressure plate will cause a slipping and not a soft pedal.
A bent fork will cause problems engaging gears and not a spongy pedal.
questions.explanation: A sticking master cylinder is the usual cause of soft or spongy pedal.

questions.question: A vehicle with a hybrid powertrain has the engine frequently starting and stopping during idle situations, even when the high-voltage battery is fully charged. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: The 12V Battery is low or failing.
feedbacks: A faulty control module could be the issue, but not the most likely.
The start/stop system is usually controlled by the 12v battery.
A bad EGR valve would cause engine performance problems.
A failed high-voltage cell would show an error code.
questions.explanation: The 12v battery runs the electronics, and the start/stop system. A low 12v battery will cause start/stop to not function properly.

questions.question: A vehicle with LED headlights has one headlight intermittently flickering or going out completely. The bulb and connector test good. What is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
feedbacks: A faulty switch would affect both lights.
The LED driver module controls the power to the light.
A relay would usually cause a full failure, and not intermittent.
A corroded ground connection will cause an intermittent problem.
questions.explanation: The two most common problems are a failing driver module or a bad ground connection.

questions.question: A vehicle's active safety features such as lane keep assist and automatic emergency braking are intermittently failing to activate or activating inappropriately. No error codes are stored. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: The cameras or sensors are dirty, damaged, or blocked
feedbacks: A brake light switch will only affect the braking system, not lane keep assist.
A blocked or dirty camera or sensor will not function correctly.
Misaligned wheel speed sensors affect the stability system.
A faulty steering angle sensor will cause stability issues.
questions.explanation: The most likely cause of intermittent active safety issues is a camera or sensor obstruction.

questions.question: A vehicle has an intermittent problem with the radio not working properly and the power windows becoming slow. What is the most common cause of this issue?
feedbacks: A faulty radio would not affect the windows.
A failing module would affect many components at once.
A faulty ignition switch will affect many systems at once.
A bad ground will affect multiple components and cause intermittent issues.
questions.explanation: A bad ground will often cause intermittent issues across multiple systems.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic parking brake (EPB) system has one rear brake refusing to release.  The EPB warning light is illuminated, and a fault code is stored.  After replacing the EPB motor on the affected side, the problem remains. What is the next most likely cause?
answers: A brake caliper that is seized
A faulty wiring harness or connector to the EPB motor
The incorrect procedure was used to replace the motor.
feedbacks: A faulty control module is not the most likely cause.
A sticking caliper will cause brake drag.
A bad connection could cause the motor to not work.
The motor was replaced correctly and should be working.
questions.explanation: A faulty connection is the most common cause of an electronic parking brake failure after replacing a motor.

questions.question: A vehicle with a continuously variable transmission (CVT) has issues with slipping and hesitation during acceleration.  The CVT fluid level is correct. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: A worn CVT belt or chain
feedbacks: A faulty TPS will cause engine performance issues.
The belt or chain is a common cause of slipping.
A faulty shift solenoid would cause incorrect gear ratios.
A faulty coolant sensor affects the engine, not the transmission.
questions.explanation: A worn or damaged belt or chain will cause a CVT to slip during acceleration.

questions.question: A customer complains of a loud whirring noise from the engine compartment that changes with engine speed. The serpentine belt and tensioner have been recently replaced.  What is the most probable cause of this noise?
feedbacks: A failing alternator bearing will cause a whirring sound.
A bad power steering pump will usually whine and not whirr.
A faulty water pump is most often a grinding noise.
A worn idler pulley is often a grinding or clicking noise.
questions.explanation: A failing alternator bearing will often make a whirring noise that changes with engine speed.

questions.question: A vehicle with an air suspension system has one corner sitting lower than the others. The air springs appear intact, and there are no visible leaks. The compressor seems to be functioning correctly, and there is no warning light illuminated. What is the most likely cause?
answers: A faulty air suspension control module
A failing air distribution valve block
A faulty ride height sensor on that corner
feedbacks: A faulty control module is not the most common cause.
A faulty valve block can cause one corner to lower.
A faulty ride sensor usually illuminates a warning light.
A faulty compressor will cause the whole system to be low, not just one corner.
questions.explanation: A failing valve block is a common reason for one corner of an air suspension system to sit lower than the others.

questions.question: A vehicle's collision avoidance system is giving false positives and activating the brakes for no reason. The sensors are clean and unobstructed. What is the most likely cause of the false positives?
feedbacks: A misaligned radar sensor can cause false positives.
A faulty yaw sensor does not cause false braking.
A bad steering angle sensor will affect other systems also.
A faulty brake light switch will not cause the collision system to engage.
questions.explanation: A misaligned radar sensor will often cause the system to believe a vehicle or object is closer than it actually is.

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic headlights are not turning off or on when they are supposed to. The headlights are working properly when manually switched. The ambient light sensor is clean, and is functioning as intended, according to a scan tool. What is the most likely issue?
feedbacks: A faulty headlight switch would affect manually turning on also.
The body control module handles the input and output of automatic lights.
A blown fuse will usually cause a lack of lights.
A faulty rain sensor will affect windshield wipers and not headlights.
questions.explanation: The body control module is usually the cause of intermittent issues with lights, after the input is tested.

questions.question: A vehicle has a misfire, and after testing, it is seen to be isolated to cylinder number 4. The spark plug, coil, and injector test good, and compression is good. What is the next most probable cause of the misfire?
feedbacks: A bad PCM is not the most likely cause of a single cylinder misfire.
A bent valve can cause a misfire on that particular cylinder.
A restricted exhaust will cause misfires on multiple cylinders.
A leaking head gasket will cause multiple misfires and not usually on one cylinder.
questions.explanation: A bent valve will usually cause a misfire on a single cylinder when all other parts test good.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic power steering (EPS) system has a clunking noise when turning the steering wheel from side to side. There are no fault codes stored. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Worn or loose steering column bushings
feedbacks: A worn tie rod end will cause play and not usually clunking.
Worn bushings will often cause clunking and movement.
A bad EPS motor is more likely to whine or not function.
A worn steering rack is more likely to cause play.
questions.explanation: Worn bushings in the steering column are a common cause of clunking in EPS systems.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) activates inappropriately at low speeds and on dry pavement. There are no fault codes stored in the ABS system. What is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: A misaligned wheel speed sensor will cause issues with the system and should be investigated.
A faulty brake pedal switch will not cause ABS to activate.
A bad steering angle sensor will cause issues with other systems also.
A bad master cylinder will not cause the system to activate.
questions.explanation: A misaligned sensor can often give a false reading to the ABS system, causing it to activate when it should not.

questions.question: A vehicle with a diesel engine has a low power issue, and the check engine light is on. The fault code P0087 is seen, which indicates low fuel rail pressure. What is the most likely cause of the error?
feedbacks: A faulty fuel pressure regulator can cause low fuel rail pressure.
A faulty crank sensor will cause no start or rough running issues.
A blocked fuel filter will also cause a low pressure reading.
A faulty injector will not cause a low pressure code.
questions.explanation: Both a faulty regulator or blocked filter can cause low fuel pressure.

questions.question: A vehicle has a clicking noise that speeds up and slows down with the vehicle's speed. It is most apparent when cornering. What is the most probable cause?
feedbacks: A worn wheel bearing will often make a humming or grinding noise.
A broken CV joint will often cause a clicking when turning.
A bad ball joint will often squeak and not click.
A loose exhaust will rattle.
questions.explanation: A clicking noise when turning is usually a sign of a worn CV joint.

questions.question: A vehicle with a turbocharged engine has a lack of power, and there is an unusual whistling sound coming from under the hood. What is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
feedbacks: A vacuum leak would not usually make a whistling noise.
A cracked intercooler will make a whistling sound.
A wastegate issue will not usually cause a whistling sound.
A blocked air filter is more likely to cause a whooshing sound.
questions.explanation: A cracked intercooler will make a whistling sound, and cause a lack of power on a turbocharged engine.

questions.question: A vehicle has an intermittent check engine light that comes on after driving for approximately 30 minutes. The code P0171 is stored, indicating the system is lean. When the car is cold, there is no light. What is the most likely cause?
feedbacks: A MAF sensor issue would cause problems hot or cold, and not usually intermittent.
A vacuum leak is more likely to cause issues when cold.
O2 sensors often fail when warm, and can cause a lean condition.
Leaking injectors will cause a rich condition, not lean.
questions.explanation: Failing O2 sensors, that fail only after being warmed, are a common cause of intermittent issues.

questions.question: A vehicle has a problem with the power windows, and they are operating very slowly. The motor has been tested and is functioning as designed. What is the most likely cause of slow operation?
answers: The window tracks are dry or dirty
feedbacks: A weak regulator will not usually cause slow operation.
A bad ground will usually cause intermittent issues, and not usually slow operation.
A failing relay would cause a no-operation issue.
Dry and dirty window tracks will cause a slowing.
questions.explanation: Dry or dirty window tracks will cause slow and noisy operation.

questions.question: A vehicle's sunroof is not functioning correctly and makes a grinding noise. It also moves very slowly and stops intermittently. What is the MOST likely cause of this problem?
answers: Worn or damaged sunroof track and guides
feedbacks: A worn motor would cause slow operation and not usually grinding.
Worn tracks and guides are often the cause of slow operation and grinding.
A switch would cause a no operation issue and not grinding or slow movement.
A relay will cause a no movement issue and not grinding or slow operation.
questions.explanation: Worn or damaged track and guides are the most likely reason for slow and grinding operation.

questions.question: A vehicle's remote start system is failing to operate correctly. It is seen to crank, but not start. The check engine light is not illuminated. What is the most likely cause?
answers: The vehicle is not in ‘P’ or ‘N’
feedbacks: A bad module would cause the system to not activate.
Remote start only works if the car is in park or neutral.
A bad crank sensor would cause no start issues, and usually an error code.
Low voltage will stop most electronic modules from functioning.
questions.explanation: Remote start will not activate if the car is not in park or neutral, and low battery voltage will also cause problems.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) warning light is constantly illuminated despite proper tire inflation. All of the sensors test good with a scan tool. What is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
answers: A bad battery in a sensor
A damaged wiring harness to the TPMS system
feedbacks: A bad control module is the most likely culprit when all else is working.
The sensors have been tested and are working correctly.
A damaged wiring will usually cause intermittent problems.
The sensors are working correctly and are the right ones.
questions.explanation: A faulty control module is the most likely reason why the TPMS system will fail if all the sensors are good.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic throttle control system has an intermittent issue with the throttle sticking. When the vehicle is scanned, no codes are present. What is the MOST likely cause of the problem?
answers: A faulty accelerator pedal position sensor
A buildup of carbon or dirt in the throttle body
feedbacks: A faulty APP sensor will affect the throttle, but not usually cause it to stick.
Carbon and dirt can cause the throttle plate to stick.
A bad ECU will cause more issues than just sticking.
A failing TPS will usually register an error code.
questions.explanation: A buildup of carbon or dirt is a common cause for throttle plates to stick in electronic throttle bodies.

questions.question: A vehicle's hybrid battery cooling system has failed, and the car has overheated. Which of the following components are the MOST likely causes?
feedbacks: A faulty coolant pump will not cool the battery, and is correct.
A faulty radiator fan may not cool the battery system.
The reservoir holds the coolant, and is correct.
The inverter coolant pump only cools the inverter, and is incorrect.
The thermistor only measures the heat, and is not the problem.
The HV module controls the operation of the system.
questions.explanation: The coolant pump, coolant reservoir and control module are all part of the battery cooling system.

questions.question: A vehicle has been experiencing a problem with the windshield wipers not working. After testing, it is seen that the wiper motor is working when power is applied, but not when activated by the switch. Which of the following are the MOST likely causes of this problem?
answers: A broken wire in the circuit
feedbacks: A faulty switch is likely cause, and is correct.
The motor was tested and is working.
A broken linkage would stop movement, but not no-operation.
A broken wire will cause a no-operation issue, and is correct.
A faulty BCM could cause issues, and is correct.
A blown fuse would be a no operation and would not allow the test to work.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is showing inaccurate readings. The sensors have been checked, and they are all within specifications. Which of the following may cause inaccurate readings?
feedbacks: Aftermarket devices are common source of interference.
The sensors were tested, and are correct.

The sensor tested good, so the battery should not be the issue.

The CAN network does control some signals, and is a possible issue.
questions.explanation: Aftermarket devices, a faulty module, and a CAN network issue can all cause the system to read incorrectly.

questions.question: A vehicle’s advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) such as lane departure warning and adaptive cruise control, are intermittently malfunctioning. Which of the following are possible causes?

Misaligned cameras will not register a correct reading.
Faulty sensors will give intermittent errors.
Worn tires do not affect ADAS.
The body control module controls the system.

questions.explanation: Dirty sensors, misaligned cameras, faulty sensors and a bad body control module can cause intermittent issues.

A bad ignition coil will cause misfires.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is not cooling effectively. The pressures are low on both the high and low side. Which of the following could be the cause of this issue?

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic transmission is slipping. Which of the following may be the cause?

Worn clutch packs will cause slipping.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) light is illuminated. Which of the following could be a possible cause of the ABS warning light being illuminated?

A faulty ABS module can cause the light to come on.
A seized caliper would not cause an ABS light to come on.
Worn brake pads will not cause an ABS light.
The steering angle sensor is not part of the ABS circuit.
questions.explanation: Bad wheel sensors, low fluid, or a bad module can all cause the ABS light.

questions.question: A vehicle with a hybrid system is exhibiting a lack of power. Which of the following components could be the cause?

questions.question: A vehicle has a very strong fuel smell. Which of the following could be the cause?

questions.question: A vehicle's power windows are not working. Which of the following are possible causes for the power windows to not operate?

A bad motor will stop the window from working.

questions.question: A modern vehicle with keyless entry has a 'no key detected' error intermittently despite a new battery in the fob. What is the next best troubleshooting step?
answers: Test the voltage output of the fob with a multimeter
Check the vehicle’s antenna locations and wiring
feedbacks: The battery was just replaced.
A voltage test may not be accurate.
A broken wire or faulty antenna could cause the issues.
Replacing the fob is a last resort option.
questions.explanation: The most common issue with keyless entry is a fault antenna or bad connection.

questions.question: A vehicle's four-wheel-drive (4WD) system engages but makes a loud grinding noise when attempting to turn sharply on dry pavement. What is the MOST likely cause of this noise?
answers: The vehicle is in 4WD on dry pavement
feedbacks: A worn chain will cause slipping, and not usually grinding.
A faulty actuator will cause a no-engagement issue.
Four-wheel-drive vehicles bind on dry pavement and grind when turning sharply.
A bad differential will cause grinding even in straight line driving.
questions.explanation: Four-wheel drive vehicles should only be used on loose surfaces. Binding will cause grinding when turning on dry surfaces.

questions.question: A vehicle with a manual transmission has excessive clutch pedal travel and a soft, spongy feel. The clutch does not slip, and the clutch fluid level is correct. What is the MOST likely cause of this problem?
feedbacks: A worn throwout bearing will cause noise and not a soft pedal.
A sticking master cylinder will cause a soft or spongy pedal feel.
A worn pressure plate will cause a slipping and not a soft pedal.
A bent fork will cause problems engaging gears and not a spongy pedal.
questions.explanation: A sticking master cylinder is the usual cause of soft or spongy pedal.

questions.question: A vehicle with a hybrid powertrain has the engine frequently starting and stopping during idle situations, even when the high-voltage battery is fully charged. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: The 12V Battery is low or failing.
feedbacks: A faulty control module could be the issue, but not the most likely.
The start/stop system is usually controlled by the 12v battery.
A bad EGR valve would cause engine performance problems.
A failed high-voltage cell would show an error code.
questions.explanation: The 12v battery runs the electronics, and the start/stop system. A low 12v battery will cause start/stop to not function properly.

questions.question: A vehicle with LED headlights has one headlight intermittently flickering or going out completely. The bulb and connector test good. What is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
feedbacks: A faulty switch would affect both lights.
The LED driver module controls the power to the light.
A relay would usually cause a full failure, and not intermittent.
A corroded ground connection will cause an intermittent problem.
questions.explanation: The two most common problems are a failing driver module or a bad ground connection.

questions.question: A vehicle's active safety features such as lane keep assist and automatic emergency braking are intermittently failing to activate or activating inappropriately. No error codes are stored. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: The cameras or sensors are dirty, damaged, or blocked
feedbacks: A brake light switch will only affect the braking system, not lane keep assist.
A blocked or dirty camera or sensor will not function correctly.
Misaligned wheel speed sensors affect the stability system.
A faulty steering angle sensor will cause stability issues.
questions.explanation: The most likely cause of intermittent active safety issues is a camera or sensor obstruction.

questions.question: A vehicle has an intermittent problem with the radio not working properly and the power windows becoming slow. What is the most common cause of this issue?
feedbacks: A faulty radio would not affect the windows.
A failing module would affect many components at once.
A faulty ignition switch will affect many systems at once.
A bad ground will affect multiple components and cause intermittent issues.
questions.explanation: A bad ground will often cause intermittent issues across multiple systems.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic parking brake (EPB) system has one rear brake refusing to release.  The EPB warning light is illuminated, and a fault code is stored.  After replacing the EPB motor on the affected side, the problem remains. What is the next most likely cause?
answers: A brake caliper that is seized
A faulty wiring harness or connector to the EPB motor
The incorrect procedure was used to replace the motor.
feedbacks: A faulty control module is not the most likely cause.
A sticking caliper will cause brake drag.
A bad connection could cause the motor to not work.
The motor was replaced correctly and should be working.
questions.explanation: A faulty connection is the most common cause of an electronic parking brake failure after replacing a motor.

questions.question: A vehicle with a continuously variable transmission (CVT) has issues with slipping and hesitation during acceleration.  The CVT fluid level is correct. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: A worn CVT belt or chain
feedbacks: A faulty TPS will cause engine performance issues.
The belt or chain is a common cause of slipping.
A faulty shift solenoid would cause incorrect gear ratios.
A faulty coolant sensor affects the engine, not the transmission.
questions.explanation: A worn or damaged belt or chain will cause a CVT to slip during acceleration.

questions.question: A customer complains of a loud whirring noise from the engine compartment that changes with engine speed. The serpentine belt and tensioner have been recently replaced.  What is the most probable cause of this noise?
feedbacks: A failing alternator bearing will cause a whirring sound.
A bad power steering pump will usually whine and not whirr.
A faulty water pump is most often a grinding noise.
A worn idler pulley is often a grinding or clicking noise.
questions.explanation: A failing alternator bearing will often make a whirring noise that changes with engine speed.

questions.question: A vehicle with an air suspension system has one corner sitting lower than the others. The air springs appear intact, and there are no visible leaks. The compressor seems to be functioning correctly, and there is no warning light illuminated. What is the most likely cause?
answers: A faulty air suspension control module
A failing air distribution valve block
A faulty ride height sensor on that corner
feedbacks: A faulty control module is not the most common cause.
A faulty valve block can cause one corner to lower.
A faulty ride sensor usually illuminates a warning light.
A faulty compressor will cause the whole system to be low, not just one corner.
questions.explanation: A failing valve block is a common reason for one corner of an air suspension system to sit lower than the others.

questions.question: A vehicle's collision avoidance system is giving false positives and activating the brakes for no reason. The sensors are clean and unobstructed. What is the most likely cause of the false positives?
feedbacks: A misaligned radar sensor can cause false positives.
A faulty yaw sensor does not cause false braking.
A bad steering angle sensor will affect other systems also.
A faulty brake light switch will not cause the collision system to engage.
questions.explanation: A misaligned radar sensor will often cause the system to believe a vehicle or object is closer than it actually is.

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic headlights are not turning off or on when they are supposed to. The headlights are working properly when manually switched. The ambient light sensor is clean, and is functioning as intended, according to a scan tool. What is the most likely issue?
feedbacks: A faulty headlight switch would affect manually turning on also.
The body control module handles the input and output of automatic lights.
A blown fuse will usually cause a lack of lights.
A faulty rain sensor will affect windshield wipers and not headlights.
questions.explanation: The body control module is usually the cause of intermittent issues with lights, after the input is tested.

questions.question: A vehicle has a misfire, and after testing, it is seen to be isolated to cylinder number 4. The spark plug, coil, and injector test good, and compression is good. What is the next most probable cause of the misfire?
feedbacks: A bad PCM is not the most likely cause of a single cylinder misfire.
A bent valve can cause a misfire on that particular cylinder.
A restricted exhaust will cause misfires on multiple cylinders.
A leaking head gasket will cause multiple misfires and not usually on one cylinder.
questions.explanation: A bent valve will usually cause a misfire on a single cylinder when all other parts test good.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic power steering (EPS) system has a clunking noise when turning the steering wheel from side to side. There are no fault codes stored. What is the MOST likely cause?
answers: Worn or loose steering column bushings
feedbacks: A worn tie rod end will cause play and not usually clunking.
Worn bushings will often cause clunking and movement.
A bad EPS motor is more likely to whine or not function.
A worn steering rack is more likely to cause play.
questions.explanation: Worn bushings in the steering column are a common cause of clunking in EPS systems.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) activates inappropriately at low speeds and on dry pavement. There are no fault codes stored in the ABS system. What is the MOST likely cause?
feedbacks: A misaligned wheel speed sensor will cause issues with the system and should be investigated.
A faulty brake pedal switch will not cause ABS to activate.
A bad steering angle sensor will cause issues with other systems also.
A bad master cylinder will not cause the system to activate.
questions.explanation: A misaligned sensor can often give a false reading to the ABS system, causing it to activate when it should not.

questions.question: A vehicle with a diesel engine has a low power issue, and the check engine light is on. The fault code P0087 is seen, which indicates low fuel rail pressure. What is the most likely cause of the error?
feedbacks: A faulty fuel pressure regulator can cause low fuel rail pressure.
A faulty crank sensor will cause no start or rough running issues.
A blocked fuel filter will also cause a low pressure reading.
A faulty injector will not cause a low pressure code.
questions.explanation: Both a faulty regulator or blocked filter can cause low fuel pressure.

questions.question: A vehicle has a clicking noise that speeds up and slows down with the vehicle's speed. It is most apparent when cornering. What is the most probable cause?
feedbacks: A worn wheel bearing will often make a humming or grinding noise.
A broken CV joint will often cause a clicking when turning.
A bad ball joint will often squeak and not click.
A loose exhaust will rattle.
questions.explanation: A clicking noise when turning is usually a sign of a worn CV joint.

questions.question: A vehicle with a turbocharged engine has a lack of power, and there is an unusual whistling sound coming from under the hood. What is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
feedbacks: A vacuum leak would not usually make a whistling noise.
A cracked intercooler will make a whistling sound.
A wastegate issue will not usually cause a whistling sound.
A blocked air filter is more likely to cause a whooshing sound.
questions.explanation: A cracked intercooler will make a whistling sound, and cause a lack of power on a turbocharged engine.

questions.question: A vehicle has an intermittent check engine light that comes on after driving for approximately 30 minutes. The code P0171 is stored, indicating the system is lean. When the car is cold, there is no light. What is the most likely cause?
feedbacks: A MAF sensor issue would cause problems hot or cold, and not usually intermittent.
A vacuum leak is more likely to cause issues when cold.
O2 sensors often fail when warm, and can cause a lean condition.
Leaking injectors will cause a rich condition, not lean.
questions.explanation: Failing O2 sensors, that fail only after being warmed, are a common cause of intermittent issues.

questions.question: A vehicle has a problem with the power windows, and they are operating very slowly. The motor has been tested and is functioning as designed. What is the most likely cause of slow operation?
answers: The window tracks are dry or dirty
feedbacks: A weak regulator will not usually cause slow operation.
A bad ground will usually cause intermittent issues, and not usually slow operation.
A failing relay would cause a no-operation issue.
Dry and dirty window tracks will cause a slowing.
questions.explanation: Dry or dirty window tracks will cause slow and noisy operation.

questions.question: A vehicle's sunroof is not functioning correctly and makes a grinding noise. It also moves very slowly and stops intermittently. What is the MOST likely cause of this problem?
answers: Worn or damaged sunroof track and guides
feedbacks: A worn motor would cause slow operation and not usually grinding.
Worn tracks and guides are often the cause of slow operation and grinding.
A switch would cause a no operation issue and not grinding or slow movement.
A relay will cause a no movement issue and not grinding or slow operation.
questions.explanation: Worn or damaged track and guides are the most likely reason for slow and grinding operation.

questions.question: A vehicle's remote start system is failing to operate correctly. It is seen to crank, but not start. The check engine light is not illuminated. What is the most likely cause?
answers: The vehicle is not in ‘P’ or ‘N’
feedbacks: A bad module would cause the system to not activate.
Remote start only works if the car is in park or neutral.
A bad crank sensor would cause no start issues, and usually an error code.
Low voltage will stop most electronic modules from functioning.
questions.explanation: Remote start will not activate if the car is not in park or neutral, and low battery voltage will also cause problems.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) warning light is constantly illuminated despite proper tire inflation. All of the sensors test good with a scan tool. What is the MOST likely cause of the issue?
answers: A bad battery in a sensor
A damaged wiring harness to the TPMS system
feedbacks: A bad control module is the most likely culprit when all else is working.
The sensors have been tested and are working correctly.
A damaged wiring will usually cause intermittent problems.
The sensors are working correctly and are the right ones.
questions.explanation: A faulty control module is the most likely reason why the TPMS system will fail if all the sensors are good.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic throttle control system has an intermittent issue with the throttle sticking. When the vehicle is scanned, no codes are present. What is the MOST likely cause of the problem?
answers: A faulty accelerator pedal position sensor
A buildup of carbon or dirt in the throttle body
feedbacks: A faulty APP sensor will affect the throttle, but not usually cause it to stick.
Carbon and dirt can cause the throttle plate to stick.
A bad ECU will cause more issues than just sticking.
A failing TPS will usually register an error code.
questions.explanation: A buildup of carbon or dirt is a common cause for throttle plates to stick in electronic throttle bodies.

questions.question: A vehicle's hybrid battery cooling system has failed, and the car has overheated. Which of the following components are the MOST likely causes?
feedbacks: A faulty coolant pump will not cool the battery, and is correct.
A faulty radiator fan may not cool the battery system.
The reservoir holds the coolant, and is correct.
The inverter coolant pump only cools the inverter, and is incorrect.
The thermistor only measures the heat, and is not the problem.
The HV module controls the operation of the system.
questions.explanation: The coolant pump, coolant reservoir and control module are all part of the battery cooling system.

questions.question: A vehicle has been experiencing a problem with the windshield wipers not working. After testing, it is seen that the wiper motor is working when power is applied, but not when activated by the switch. Which of the following are the MOST likely causes of this problem?
answers: A broken wire in the circuit
feedbacks: A faulty switch is likely cause, and is correct.
The motor was tested and is working.
A broken linkage would stop movement, but not no-operation.
A broken wire will cause a no-operation issue, and is correct.
A faulty BCM could cause issues, and is correct.
A blown fuse would be a no operation and would not allow the test to work.
questions.explanation: The most common reasons for the wipers to not work, even when the motor is ok, are the switch, wiring and body control module.

questions.question: A vehicle's tire pressure monitoring system (TPMS) is showing inaccurate readings. The sensors have been checked, and they are all within specifications. Which of the following may cause inaccurate readings?
feedbacks: Aftermarket devices are common source of interference.
The sensors were tested, and are correct.
The module is a likely cause of bad readings.
The sensor tested good, so the battery should not be the issue.
Over or under inflation will give a correct reading of the bad pressure.
The CAN network does control some signals, and is a possible issue.
questions.explanation: Aftermarket devices, a faulty module, and a CAN network issue can all cause the system to read incorrectly.

questions.question: A vehicle’s advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) such as lane departure warning and adaptive cruise control, are intermittently malfunctioning. Which of the following are possible causes?
feedbacks: A dirty or obstructed sensor will not function correctly.
Misaligned cameras will not register a correct reading.
Faulty sensors will give intermittent errors.
Worn tires do not affect ADAS.
The body control module controls the system.
Low pressure will affect traction, but not ADAS.
questions.explanation: Dirty sensors, misaligned cameras, faulty sensors and a bad body control module can cause intermittent issues.

questions.question: A vehicle with a four-wheel-drive (4WD) system experiences binding when turning on dry pavement. Which of the following components may be causing this issue if the vehicle is in 4WD mode?
feedbacks: A faulty transfer case will often not lock into 4WD, but not bind.
Worn CV joints do not cause binding.
A faulty locking differential can cause the system to bind.
Mismatched tire sizes can cause a binding issue.
A worn limited slip differential will cause slipping and not binding.
A wheel speed sensor will not cause binding.
questions.explanation: A faulty locking differential, or mismatched tire sizes will cause binding on dry pavement.

questions.question: A vehicle has a parasitic draw that is draining the battery overnight. Which of the following methods would MOST effectively isolate the source of the parasitic draw?
answers: Using a multimeter to measure current at each fuse
Disconnecting electrical components one at a time
Using a scan tool to read current draws
Using a thermal camera to identify hot spots
Checking for corrosion on ground connections
feedbacks: This would identify the specific circuit.
Melted wires are not necessarily a parasitic draw.
A method that will identify which component is causing the draw.
Scan tools cannot read current draws.
Not an effective way to measure current draw.
Corrosion would cause a high resistance and not a parasitic draw.
questions.explanation: Using a multimeter on the fuses and disconnecting components are effective ways to identify a parasitic draw.

questions.question: A vehicle's engine is misfiring. Which of the following are potential causes of the misfire?
feedbacks: A faulty spark plug will cause a misfire.
A bad ignition coil will cause misfires.
A bad cam sensor will cause running issues.
A vacuum leak can cause misfires.
Low fuel pressure will cause misfires.
A worn timing chain will cause timing issues and misfires.
questions.explanation: Any of these will cause a misfire in the engine.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is not cooling effectively. The pressures are low on both the high and low side. Which of the following could be the cause of this issue?
feedbacks: A leak would cause low pressure on both sides.
A faulty compressor will cause pressures to drop.
A blockage is more likely to cause a high pressure.
A bad expansion valve would not usually cause low pressures on both sides.
A bad fan would cause high pressures.
An overcharged system will give high pressures.
questions.explanation: A refrigerant leak and a failing compressor will cause low pressures on both sides.

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic transmission is slipping. Which of the following may be the cause?
answers: A bad input or output speed sensor
feedbacks: Low fluid is the most common reason for slipping.
Worn clutch packs will cause slipping.
A faulty solenoid will cause shifting problems and slipping.
A TPS issue will not cause slipping.
A speed sensor will not cause slipping.
Worn shift forks will cause slipping.
questions.explanation: Low fluid, worn clutches, a bad solenoid, or worn shift forks can cause slipping.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) light is illuminated. Which of the following could be a possible cause of the ABS warning light being illuminated?
feedbacks: A bad wheel speed sensor is a common cause of the ABS light.
Low fluid will often trigger the ABS warning light.
A faulty ABS module can cause the light to come on.
A seized caliper would not cause an ABS light to come on.
Worn brake pads will not cause an ABS light.
The steering angle sensor is not part of the ABS circuit.
questions.explanation: Bad wheel sensors, low fluid, or a bad module can all cause the ABS light.

questions.question: A vehicle with a hybrid system is exhibiting a lack of power. Which of the following components could be the cause?
feedbacks: A bad HV battery can cause a lack of power.
A bad 12V battery will not usually cause a lack of power.
A faulty inverter can cause a lack of power.
A bad electric motor can cause a lack of power.
A bad EGR will not cause lack of power.
A clogged catalyst will cause a lack of power.
questions.explanation: A faulty high voltage battery, inverter, electric motor, or clogged catalyst will all cause a lack of power.

questions.question: A vehicle has a very strong fuel smell. Which of the following could be the cause?
feedbacks: A leaking fuel line will cause a fuel smell.
Leaking injectors can cause a smell of fuel.
A leaking EVAP canister will cause a fuel smell.
A MAF sensor is not usually the reason for a smell of fuel.
A cracked cylinder head will not usually cause a fuel smell.
A clogged air filter will not cause a fuel smell.
questions.explanation: Leaking fuel lines, injectors, and EVAP canisters are the most common causes of a strong fuel smell.

questions.question: A vehicle's power windows are not working. Which of the following are possible causes for the power windows to not operate?
feedbacks: A blown fuse will stop the windows from working.
A bad motor will stop the window from working.
A bad regulator would cause the window to not move.
A bad switch would cause the windows to not operate.
The body control module controls the power windows.
A bad ground will cause a no operation.
questions.explanation: A blown fuse, bad motor, bad regulator, bad switch, bad module, or bad ground will all cause the power windows to not operate.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic throttle control system is experiencing a fault with the throttle plate not returning to idle. Which of the following could be the cause of this problem?
answers: A build up of carbon or dirt on the throttle plate
A faulty accelerator pedal position sensor
feedbacks: A build up of carbon can cause sticking.
A bad APP sensor will not cause sticking.
A bad TPS is a possibility.
A faulty spring will stop the throttle from returning.
A bad PCM is not the first thing to suspect.
A vacuum leak will affect the idle, but not stick it.
questions.explanation: Carbon buildup, a faulty TPS or a return spring can stop the throttle plate from returning to idle.

questions.question: A vehicle with a remote start system is failing to operate. Which of the following could be the causes of the remote start not working?
answers: The check engine light is illuminated
The vehicle is not in park or neutral
feedbacks: Low voltage will cause many systems to stop working.
The system will not work if there is a check engine light.
The vehicle must be in park or neutral.
Most remote start systems have a safety feature that stops it working with the hood open.
A faulty module will stop the system from working.
A low fob battery can affect operation of the remote start.
questions.explanation: All of these conditions will stop a remote start from functioning correctly.

questions.question: A vehicle's electronic stability control (ESC) system is activating incorrectly. Which of the following components could cause this system to activate incorrectly?
feedbacks: A misaligned wheel speed sensor can give a false reading.
A bad steering sensor can make the car believe it is turning more than it actually is.
A faulty yaw sensor will give a false signal.
A faulty brake light switch is not part of the ESC system.
A worn rack does not usually cause issues with the ESC system.
A faulty ABS module is a part of the stability system.
questions.explanation: A misaligned wheel sensor or steering sensor, a bad yaw sensor, or a bad ABS module can all cause stability system issues.

questions.question: A vehicle with an air suspension system has a fault with a single corner sagging. Which of the following could cause a single corner to sag?
answers: A leak in the air spring on that corner
A faulty ride height sensor on that corner
A faulty air line on that corner
feedbacks: A leak would cause that corner to sag.
A bad height sensor would not usually cause the corner to sag.
A bad valve can cause one corner to be lower.
A faulty compressor will usually cause all the corners to be low.
A leak in the line will also cause that corner to drop.
A bad module would cause issues on multiple corners.
questions.explanation: A leak in the air spring or line, and a bad distribution valve are common causes of one corner being low.

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic headlights are failing to turn on or off when they should. Which of the following could cause the headlights to not function correctly?
answers: A broken wire in the circuit
feedbacks: A bad sensor will not trigger the system.
A bad switch will cause the headlights to not turn on.
A faulty BCM can cause problems with the system.
A bad relay will cause the lights to not activate.
A bad ground will stop many systems from working.
A broken wire can stop the lights from working.
questions.explanation: A faulty ambient light sensor, switch, body control module, relay, ground, or broken wire can all cause the headlights to malfunction.

questions.question: A vehicle has an issue with the power windows operating very slowly. Which of the following could cause slow operation of the power windows?
feedbacks: Dry tracks will slow the operation.
A regulator will not cause slow operation.
A worn motor will not usually cause slow operation.
A bad ground connection will often stop the windows from working.
A relay will not usually cause slow operation.
A bad switch will usually stop operation.
questions.explanation: Dry or dirty window tracks are a common reason for slow operation.

questions.question: A vehicle's power steering system is experiencing issues with whining and resistance. Which of the following components could cause this issue?
answers: A clogged power steering fluid reservoir
feedbacks: Low fluid will often cause whining and resistance.
A bad pump will cause noise and resistance.
A loose belt can slip and cause noise and resistance.
Worn bushings will cause play.
A clogged reservoir would stop the flow of fluid and cause noise.
A bad steering angle sensor would not cause noise or resistance.
questions.explanation: Low fluid, a bad pump, loose belt or clogged reservoir can cause whining and resistance.

questions.question: A vehicle's charging system is experiencing low voltage output. Which of the following could be the cause?
feedbacks: A bad alternator will stop charging.
A worn belt will slip and cause low charging.
A bad battery will not hold a charge.
A bad regulator will not allow the system to charge.
A blown fuse will stop the charging process.
A bad ground will cause low voltage issues.
questions.explanation: A bad alternator, belt, battery, regulator, fuse or ground will all cause a low output voltage.

questions.question: A vehicle's automatic transmission is shifting harshly. Which of the following could cause harsh shifting?
feedbacks: A bad solenoid will cause shifting issues.
Low fluid will cause slipping, but may also cause harsh shifts.
A bad TCM will cause shifting problems.
A TPS will not cause harsh shifting.
Worn clutches usually cause slipping and not usually harsh shifts.
A bad linkage can cause shifting problems.
questions.explanation: A faulty solenoid or module, low fluid, and a bad linkage can all cause harsh shifts.

questions.question: A vehicle with an electronic parking brake (EPB) has a fault with one of the rear brakes not releasing. Which of the following could be the cause?
answers: An incorrect procedure used to replace the motor
feedbacks: A bad motor will not release.
A seized caliper will also cause the brake to not release.
A bad module can cause the system to not work.
A bad harness can stop the power getting to the EPB motor.
A worn pad will not cause a no release.
An incorrect procedure will cause the brakes not to work properly.
questions.explanation: A faulty motor, caliper, module, wiring, or incorrect procedure will all cause a brake to not release.

questions.question: A vehicle has a very high fuel consumption. Which of the following could be the reason for high fuel consumption?
feedbacks: A clogged filter is a possible reason.
Leaking injectors will cause high fuel usage.
A bad MAF sensor can cause high fuel usage.
A bad O2 sensor will cause high fuel consumption.
A bad coolant temperature sensor can cause high consumption.
Low pressure will cause the car to work harder but will not greatly increase consumption.
questions.explanation: A clogged filter, leaking injectors, a bad MAF, O2 or coolant temperature sensor will all cause high fuel usage.

questions.question: A vehicle's air conditioning system is blowing warm air. Which of the following could be the cause of this issue?
feedbacks: Low charge will cause the air to not be cold.
A faulty compressor will stop the AC system from cooling.
A bad expansion valve will cause the system to not cool.
A faulty actuator will not move the door.
A clogged condenser would cause high pressures.
A bad resistor would stop the blower from working and not cause warm air.
questions.explanation: Low charge, bad compressor or expansion valve, and a bad blend door actuator can all cause a lack of cold air.

questions.question: A vehicle's suspension system is experiencing clunking noises. Which of the following could be the cause?
feedbacks: Worn end links are a common cause of noise.
Worn mounts will cause noise.
Worn ball joints will cause noise.
Worn wheel bearings will cause humming.
Worn tie rod ends will not usually clunk.
Worn control arm bushings will also cause clunking.
questions.explanation: Worn sway bar links, strut mounts, ball joints or control arm bushings will all cause clunking noises.

questions.question: A vehicle's anti-lock braking system (ABS) is activating at low speeds and on dry surfaces. Which of the following could cause this issue?
feedbacks: A misaligned sensor will give a bad reading.
A bad wheel speed sensor will cause the system to activate.
A bad steering sensor could cause stability issues and activation.
A bad brake switch will not usually cause the system to activate.
Worn brake pads will not cause this.
A bad module could cause the system to activate.
questions.explanation: A misaligned or bad wheel sensor, bad steering sensor, or a bad ABS module can all cause this issue.

questions.question: A vehicle with a turbocharged engine has a lack of power and unusual noises. Which of the following could be the cause?
feedbacks: A boost leak will cause a lack of power and noise.
A bad wastegate can cause a lack of power.
A worn turbo can cause noises and lack of power.
A blocked air filter is not a usual cause.
A leaking EGR valve will not cause noises.
A faulty TPS would cause engine running problems, not usually low power.
questions.explanation: A boost leak, bad wastegate actuator, or a worn turbocharger can cause low power and unusual noises.

questions.question: A vehicle with a diesel engine has a lack of power and is producing black smoke. Which of the following are potential causes?
feedbacks: Leaking injectors will cause black smoke.
A bad EGR will not cause black smoke.
A restricted filter will cause black smoke.
A bad turbo will cause a lack of power.
A bad MAF will not cause black smoke.
A clogged exhaust will cause a lack of power.
questions.explanation: Leaking injectors, a restricted filter, bad turbo, or a clogged exhaust will cause a lack of power and black smoke.

questions.question: A vehicle's lane departure warning system (LDWS) is malfunctioning. Which of the following could be the cause of the malfunctions?
feedbacks: A misaligned camera can cause the system to not function correctly.
A dirty camera will not function.
The lane markings affect the system.
A bad steering sensor will give bad readings.
Worn tires will not affect LDWS.
A bad rain sensor does not affect lane departure.
questions.explanation: A misaligned camera, dirty lenses, faulty lane markings or bad steering sensor will all cause issues with the LDWS.

questions.question: A vehicle with a continuously variable transmission (CVT) is slipping and hesitating. Which of the following could be the causes?
answers: A worn CVT belt or chain
A bad input or output speed sensor
feedbacks: A worn belt will cause slipping.
A bad solenoid will cause shifting issues.
